  "text": "Every Thursday, Martin borrowed the library’s newspaper and read the shipping forecast, though the town lay eighty miles from the sea.

“You could take it home,” the librarian said.

“Then I’d have to bring it back.”

“You come back anyway.”

He folded the page along its old crease.

One Thursday his usual chair was occupied by a girl with a trumpet case. She had spread her homework across the table.

Martin sat by the radiator instead.

The following week she was there again.

“Is this your place?” she asked.

“Not officially.”

She moved her books. He sat down.

For several weeks they worked without speaking, except when she asked how to spell Mediterranean. He checked the newspaper before answering.

In December she arrived without the trumpet.

“Given it up?” he asked.

“It’s being repaired. The valve sticks.”

“My brother played.”

“Was he good?”

“He was loud.”

She smiled, then returned to her sums.

The next Thursday Martin brought a narrow bottle of valve oil. The label had peeled at one corner.

“This might be no use now,” he said.

She turned it over carefully.

“I’ll ask my teacher.”

After Christmas, a small envelope lay on his chair. Inside was a ticket for a school concert.

“Saturday,” the girl said. “You don’t have to.”

Martin checked the time printed beneath the school crest.

“Will it be loud?”

“Probably.”

He tucked the ticket into his wallet.

On Saturday he arrived early. The hall smelled of floor polish. He chose a seat halfway back and left his coat on the chair beside him until the room began to fill."
